children: and commodities ​trader Mercuria Energy are among firms interested in a ‌potential deal for Venezuela's largest aluminum smelter, Bloomberg reported Friday.

The two companies are each in discussions with the Venezuelan government about ​a deal for the Venalum smelter, and while it is not clear what structure any agreement might involve, talks have included ​operating the facility and gaining access to the aluminum ⁠it produces, according to the report.

Venalum is controlled by the Venezuelan state and was once a major aluminum producer whose output collapsed after years of under-investment, power shortages, and economic turmoil; it has a capacity to produce 430K tons/year of primary aluminum.
